subtitle: std::array<T,N> — C++11's fixed-size aggregate sequence container. restd back-ports the class itself to C++98 as a structural aggregate (public _M_elems C-array member, internal::array_storage helper for the zero-size case), with the constexpr surface matched to std's progression (size/empty/max_size from C++11; const accessors and get<I> from C++14 per LWG 2185; non-const accessors from C++17; fill and member swap from C++20). The six legacy comparison operators are restd-ahead-of-std: explicit overloads ship on every tier and are constexpr from C++14 (std waited for C++20 / P1614). to_array is back-ported to C++11+ (needs variadic templates, rvalue references, and integer_sequence — all now satisfied) and is constexpr-from-introduction. The CTAD deduction guide and operator<=> are C++17 and C++20 language features respectively and cannot be back-ported further. The three-way overload matches the tuple module's simplification — element types without their own <=> produce a compile error at the decltype site (no synth-three-way fallback).
legend_blurb: Per-symbol coverage of the C++ <array> header (C++11). Implemented; class on C++98+, to_array on C++11+, CTAD on C++17+, operator<=> on C++20+. Comparison operators are constexpr from C++14 (ahead of std).

symbols.name: array<T,N>
symbols.notes: Aggregate struct with a public _M_elems[_Size] storage member (required for C++98 brace-init: aggregate rules forbid private/protected non-static data members). Zero-size case is handled via internal::array_storage<_Type, _Size> — a partial specialisation for _Size == 0 holds a single placeholder element and returns nullptr from data(); same workaround used by libstdc++ and libc++. Iterator and const_iterator are raw _Type*/const _Type* pointers (matches libstdc++/libc++); reverse_iterator pairs use restd::reverse_iterator. Constexpr surface matches std: size/empty/max_size from C++11; const accessors (operator[], at, front, back, data, begin, end, cbegin, cend, rbegin, rend, crbegin, crend) from C++14 per LWG 2185; non-const accessors from C++17; fill and member swap from C++20. at() throws std::out_of_range when D_ENV_CPP98_HAS_STDEXCEPT, std::exception when only D_ENV_CPP98_HAS_EXCEPTION, no-op (UB) otherwise — matches libstdc++ -fno-exceptions.

symbols.name: get<I>(array)
symbols.notes: Lives in array_get.hpp. Four value-category overloads on C++11+: get<I>(array&), get<I>(const array&), get<I>(array&&), get<I>(const array&&) — last three gated on D_ENV_CPP_FEATURE_LANG_RVALUE_REFERENCES. On C++98/03 only the two lvalue overloads ship. Bounds check via static_assert (C++11+); silently UB on C++98/03 out-of-range. Constexpr from C++14 (LWG 2185) — non-const reference returns were not legal from C++11 constexpr bodies.

symbols.name: operator== (array)
symbols.notes: Lives in array_compare.hpp. Element-wise equality via for-loop (early exit on first mismatch). RESTD AHEAD OF STD: constexpr from C++14 (relaxed-constexpr rules permit loops in function bodies); std didn't make this constexpr until C++20 / P1614.

symbols.name: operator!= (array)
symbols.notes: Defined as !(_lhs == _rhs). Synthesised from operator<=> in std since C++20; restd keeps the explicit overload on every tier so C++11–C++17 code can still rely on it. RESTD AHEAD OF STD: constexpr from C++14.

symbols.name: operator< (array)
symbols.notes: Lexicographic less-than via element-wise for-loop. Zero-size arrays compare equal so op< returns false. RESTD AHEAD OF STD: constexpr from C++14.

symbols.name: operator<= (array)
symbols.notes: Defined as !(_rhs < _lhs) — canonical reflection through op<. Synthesised in std since C++20; restd keeps explicit. RESTD AHEAD OF STD: constexpr from C++14.

symbols.name: operator> (array)
symbols.notes: Defined as _rhs < _lhs. Synthesised in std since C++20; restd keeps explicit. RESTD AHEAD OF STD: constexpr from C++14.

symbols.name: operator>= (array)
symbols.notes: Defined as !(_lhs < _rhs). Synthesised in std since C++20; restd keeps explicit. RESTD AHEAD OF STD: constexpr from C++14.

symbols.name: operator<=> (array)
symbols.notes: Lives in array_compare_three_way.hpp; gated on D_ENV_LANG_IS_CPP20_OR_HIGHER. Lexicographic three-way comparison; result type derived via decltype(declval<T const&>() <=> declval<T const&>()). Mirrors the tuple module's simplification — no synth-three-way fallback; element types lacking their own <=> produce a compile error at the decltype site (deliberate; matches restd::tuple's back-port decision).
symbols.failure_reason: operator<=> is a C++20 language feature; cannot be back-ported to earlier tiers. The six legacy relational operators in array_compare.hpp cover C++11–C++17 use cases.

symbols.name: swap (array)
symbols.notes: ADL-friendly non-member swap delegating to the member swap (which does an element-wise copy-swap). is_swappable_v / is_nothrow_swappable_v constraints omitted relative to std — _Type's swappability is enforced naturally at instantiation of the member swap. Constexpr from C++20 (matches std P1023).

symbols.name: to_array
symbols.notes: Lives in to_array.hpp; gated on D_ENV_CPP_FEATURE_LANG_VARIADIC_TEMPLATES && D_ENV_CPP_FEATURE_LANG_RVALUE_REFERENCES (effectively C++11+). Two overloads: to_array(T (&)[N]) copies elements, to_array(T (&&)[N]) moves them. Both return array<remove_cv_t<T>, N>. Multidimensional input rejected via static_assert(!restd::is_array<T>::value). Implemented via restd::make_index_sequence expansion. RESTD AHEAD OF STD: ships on C++11+ (std waited for C++20) and constexpr from introduction.
symbols.failure_reason: Cannot reach C++98 — implementation requires variadic templates, rvalue references, and index_sequence expansion, all C++11+ language features. C++98/03 users construct arrays directly via aggregate brace-init.

symbols.name: tuple_size<array>
symbols.notes: Lives in array_tuple_size.hpp. tuple_size<array<T,N>> inherits from restd::integral_constant<size_t, N>. Cv-qualified passthrough handled by the primary tuple_size template's existing specialisations (LWG 2762) in restd::utility.

symbols.name: tuple_element<I, array>
symbols.notes: Lives in array_tuple_element.hpp. tuple_element<I, array<T,N>>::type == T. static_assert on I < N (C++11+); C++98 omits the assert (substitution failure at use site). Cv-qualified passthrough handled by primary tuple_element in restd::utility.

symbols.name: array deduction guide
symbols.notes: Defined at the bottom of array.hpp; gated on D_ENV_LANG_IS_CPP17_OR_HIGHER. Signature: array(T, Rest...) -> array<T, 1 + sizeof...(Rest)> with a fold-expression SFINAE constraint (restd::is_same<_Type, _Rest>::value && ...) enforcing element homogeneity — the C++17 standard's own approach (C++17 deduction guides can't carry requires-clauses). CTAD is a language feature; cannot be back-ported to C++11–C++14.
symbols.failure_reason: CTAD (class template argument deduction) is a C++17 language feature; cannot be back-ported. C++11–C++14 users specify the array's element type and extent explicitly: restd::array<int, 3> a = {1, 2, 3};
